item: glass-expansion (Android port, branch android-int-oct3): more Liquid Glass in glass mode. Queue toolbar as separate glass circles, the queue as a ~92 % glass sheet with the player visible above it, and the ⋯ button morphing into the menu pills. Song options, AI Daily Mix and Taizo sheets get the same treatment. Primary buttons on floating bars (Save as playlist, Edit song, tab-order Done, Quick Fill Next) become glass pills. The Listening Stats header becomes a frosted bar like Settings. Then an audit of the remaining non-glass surfaces. Lyrics page and full-player top bar are out of scope.
currentBehaviour:
Every citation below was read at /home/user/android-wt/base (HEAD 90d32ca). Nothing was compiled: ANDROID_HOME is unset here.

HOW ANDROID GLASS WORKS, AND HOW IT DIFFERS FROM iOS
- Glass in the NexHome kit refracts only the baked album-art ambient layer. The root records that one layer (GlassModeRoot.kt:22-37, 66-76). Sheets and dialogs in other windows draw a window-aligned copy of it (GlassWindowBackdrop.kt:18-37).
- FlattenNestedGlass = true (GlassLocals.kt:36-47), so glass never refracts other glass or app content.
- The lyrics precedent says the same thing: "sampling the artwork background … never the lyric lines" (LyricsSheet.kt:666-670).
- So on Android "see-through" can only mean "refracts the ambient, with the player visible around the sheet". A partial-height sheet over the player can't show the player's art or controls through the glass, as it can on iOS.

QUEUE TODAY (glass mode)
- Layout: full screen, in the same window as the player. QueueBottomSheet is laid out with fillMaxSize (UnifiedPlayerOverlaysLayer.kt:151-166).
- The header pads by the status bar plus 10 dp (QueueBottomSheet.kt:803-805).
- Background: the queue has no container of its own (QueueBottomSheet.kt:753-755, 796-797). It sits on GlassSheetScrim, which becomes opaque at full open (UnifiedPlayerOverlaysLayer.kt:117-125; GlassSheetScaffold.kt:230-253).
- Because that scrim is opaque, the full player is hidden at full open. Alpha drops to 0 and its glass reads an empty backdrop: glassQueueCoversPlayerProvider (UnifiedPlayerSheetV2.kt:101, 561-565, 860), UnifiedPlayerSheetLayers.kt:211, 241-251.
- Toolbar: three flat 48 dp kit circles (GlassQueueToolbarButton, QueueBottomSheet.kt:1635-1681) inside one tintStrong GlassPanel capsule. That is glass-on-glass (1596-1613). The ⋯ is a separate 64 dp GlassCircleAction (1026-1033).
- ⋯ menu: not glass in glass mode.
  - It is three Material Surfaces with opaque tertiary/error/primary containers. `QueueToolbarMenuButton` is at 1265-1312, the pills are laid out at 1098-1163, and the colours are raw player-scheme colours because PlayerSchemeMaterialTheme doesn't remap for glass (PlayerSchemeScopes.kt:37-47).
  - They sit over a 0.55 Material scrim (1057-1074) and a gradient to an opaque surfaceContainerLowest (1076-1096).
  - The menu slides and fades in; there is no morph.
- Other non-glass parts of the queue:
  - The undo bar is an inverseSurface Surface (1168-1219).
  - The source badge is surfaceContainerHighest @ 0.88 (1441-1474).
  - The empty-state text uses the player scheme's onSurface (840-843).
  - The swipe-to-remove reveal is a plain errorContainer background (around 2184-2219). Leave it, as iOS did: a lens per row created mid-gesture is too costly.

SONG OPTIONS, AI DAILY MIX, TAIZO: ALREADY DONE
- All three are AdaptiveModalBottomSheet. In glass mode that is a heavy GlassPanel container (tintStrong, lens 24/48) over the window-aligned ambient, under the palette scrim (GlassAdaptive.kt:278-386).
- None of them is full height:
  - Taizo chat: heightIn(360..620 dp) (TaisChatSheet.kt:107-118).
  - Song options: the pager is capped at screen height − insets − 180 dp (SongInfoBottomSheet.kt:370-388).
  - AI Daily Mix: a content-sized scrolling column (AiPlaylistSheet.kt:187-198).
- The player or page already shows above them. The iOS problem (full-height sheets turning opaque) doesn't exist on Android.

FLOATING BARS
- Save as playlist: an AdaptiveFullScreenDialog (QueueBottomSheet.kt:1763-1770). Its bar is a secondaryContainer Surface (60 % in glass) holding a solid primary Button (1923-2009).
- Edit song: a HorizontalFloatingToolbar with a FilledTonalButton Cancel and a Button Save (EditSongSheet.kt:725-779). It is hosted in AdaptiveFullScreenDialog (136-156).
- Reorder tabs: FloatingToolBar, a surfaceContainerHigh box with a reset IconButton and a MediumExtendedFloatingActionButton Done (ReorderTabsSheet.kt:235-288). It sits in a glass AdaptiveModalBottomSheet (129-133).
- Quick Fill: a surfaceContainerHighest Surface with segmented FilledTonalButtons and a primary Button Next/Apply, enabled = isNextEnabled (QuickFillScreen.kt:191-302). It is hosted in AdaptiveFullScreenDialog (59-72).

STATS: ALREADY MATCHES SETTINGS
- The Stats header in glass mode is the same as Settings:
  - the floating GlassTopBar capsule via CollapsibleCommonTopBar → GlassCollapsingTopBar (CollapsibleCommonTopBar.kt:75-91; ScreenChrome.kt:112-147);
  - the band fills with the aligned ambient as it collapses: glassAwareHeaderFill (StatsScreen.kt:359-366; GlassScreens.kt:132-143);
  - refresh is a GlassCircleAction (StatsScreen.kt:376-390) and the range tabs are a GlassTabStrip (679-692).
- Settings uses the same CollapsibleCommonTopBar (SettingsScreen.kt:340-343).
- Material mode: both screens use a surfaceContainerHigh band at the same alpha.
- The iOS "solid band" divergence doesn't exist on Android.

NON-GLASS SURFACES IN GLASS MODE (most visible first)
1. Full player, the song-info row (not the top bar): the buffering LoadingIndicator in a Surface (FullPlayerContent.kt:1729-1771), the lyrics|queue split chips (1773-1820), the lyrics FilledIconButton (1821-1837) and the Taizo circle (1839-1855). All are solid chipColor fills (chipColor = onAccent @ 0.8, 662/686).
2. Queue: menu, undo bar and badge (above).
3. Screen FABs: the Genre options MediumFloatingActionButton (GenreDetailScreen.kt:482-493), the Daily Mix AI LargeExtendedFloatingActionButton (DailyMixScreen.kt:573-586), and Create/Save playlist MediumExtendedFloatingActionButtons (CreatePlaylistScreen.kt:447, 875). They are translucent tinted fills with shadow.
4. The player's file-info pill: a textColor @ 0.14 Surface (FullPlayerContent.kt:2300-2320).
5. The Genre artist/album header tiles (GenreDetailScreen.kt:867-1000). These are glass-remapped translucent fills behind rows; leave them, as iOS did.

KIT FACTS THE PLAN DEPENDS ON
- GlassPanel builds its drawBackdrop chain once per real input (GlassPanel.kt:102-176).
- LiquidButton rebuilds it on every recomposition (LiquidButton.kt:84-135). Pills on screens with text fields must use GlassPanel, not LiquidButton.
- InteractiveHighlight only inspects pointers and never consumes them (utils/InteractiveHighlight.kt:32). Glass buttons inside the queue's drag areas are safe.
- Full-player realtime updates already stop once the queue is at least 8 % open (FullPlayerRuntimePolicy.kt:34-45).
- Verified in this environment's Gradle cache, by running javap on material3-android 1.5.0-alpha22 classes.jar: `FloatingActionButtonMenu(Boolean, @Composable () -> Unit, Modifier, Alignment.Horizontal, @Composable FloatingActionButtonMenuScope.() -> Unit)`, `FloatingActionButtonMenuScope.FloatingActionButtonMenuItem(onClick, text, icon, Modifier, containerColor, contentColor)`, `ToggleFloatingActionButton(Boolean, (Boolean) -> Unit, Modifier, (Float) -> Color, Alignment, (Float) -> Dp, (Float) -> Dp, ToggleFloatingActionButtonScope.() -> Unit)` with `checkedProgress`, and `ToggleFloatingActionButtonDefaults.animateIcon(...)`. These carry no ExperimentalMaterial3ExpressiveApi marker in the bytecode; QueueBottomSheet already opts in anyway (229-231).
alreadyOnAndroid:
- **Queue:** the header is a heavy glass panel (QueueBottomSheet.kt:1345-1365), the now-playing row is a light panel and the other rows are flat with a press swell (2247-2266). The toolbar is glass (1596-1613), ⋯ is a glass orb (1026-1033), and the lenses bloom with the open progress (UnifiedPlayerOverlaysLayer.kt:141-150).
- **Song options, AI Daily Mix and Taizo chat:** already partial-height glass sheets over a see-through palette scrim (GlassAdaptive.kt:346-385; TaisChatSheet.kt:116; SongInfoBottomSheet.kt:372-377; AiPlaylistSheet.kt:193-198). They need no change in either mode.
- **Listening Stats header:** already the same glass bar as Settings in both modes (StatsScreen.kt:359-416; CollapsibleCommonTopBar.kt:75-91; SettingsScreen.kt:340). It needs no change.
- **Floating-bar hosts:** Save as playlist, Edit song and Quick Fill already sit in glass full-screen dialogs (AdaptiveFullScreenDialog, GlassAdaptive.kt:602-629), and Reorder tabs in a glass sheet. Only their bar buttons are still Material fills.
- **Material mode:** already has M3 floating toolbars with filled primary buttons on those bars, and standard partial-height modal sheets for the three sheets.

recommendedPlan.change:
Extend GlassCircleAction (97-127), keeping its existing look as the default, with three optional parameters:
- `lit: () -> Float = { 0f }`: the accent flood and rim of the queue toolbar's on state, using the NexHome chip recipe in QueueBottomSheet.kt:1663-1676 (accent@0.9 BlendMode.Hue, then accent@0.42, then a 1 dp accent@0.8 circle stroke). Draw it through GlassPanel's `onDrawSurface` / `onDrawFront`, which are child layers (GlassPanel.kt:205-213), never inside the glass node, so toggling and the GlowSpring don't re-render the lens. Read `lit()` only inside those draw lambdas.
- `enterProgress: () -> Float = { 1f }`: passed through to GlassPanel for the lens-bloom materialize.
- `pressScale` stays LiquidMotion.OrbPressScale.
Pass remembered lambdas: GlassPanel captures them with rememberUpdatedState.

Add the shared-element morph used by the queue ⋯ menu:
- `fun Modifier.glassMorphBounds(from: () -> Rect, to: () -> Rect, progress: () -> Float): Modifier`, implemented with `Modifier.layout { measurable, _ -> }`. It reads `progress()` in the LAYOUT phase only, measures the child with fixed constraints equal to the lerped size, and places it at the lerped offset. Layout reads do not recompose.
- Pure helpers: `internal fun lerpMorphRect(from: Rect, to: Rect, p: Float): Rect`, which clamps p to [0,1] for geometry so the spring overshoot can't invert sizes (uses androidx.compose.ui.geometry.lerp(Rect, Rect, Float)); `internal fun morphFadeOut(p: Float, end: Float = 0.4f)`; `internal fun morphFadeIn(p: Float, start: Float = 0.5f)`.
- LiquidMotion tokens: `MorphOpenSpring = spring(dampingRatio = 0.72f, stiffness = 360f, visibilityThreshold = 0.001f)` and `MorphCloseSpring = spring(dampingRatio = 1f, stiffness = 520f, visibilityThreshold = 0.001f)`. EnterSpring (0.62/170) is too slow for a menu.
- Shape stays Capsule for the whole morph: a 64×64 capsule is the circle and a 230×56 capsule is the pill. The GlassPanel modifier is therefore never rebuilt; only its size changes. That re-renders one lens per frame for about 300 ms.
- Never put `layerBackdrop` on any ancestor of the morphing node.

Make the queue a ~92 % sheet in BOTH modes.

risks: The Android kit can't make the queue truly see-through. Glass refracts only the baked ambient (GlassLocals.kt:10-47; GlassModeRoot.kt:22-37), so the 92 % sheet shows the player above it and the album-art ambient through it, not the player's art or controls. Recording the full player into a layerBackdrop the queue samples is legal, because they are siblings, but it breaks FlattenNestedGlass: a glass-on-glass chain plus a ~full-screen lens re-rendered on every player redraw, the 170–275 ms GPU frames noted in GlassLocals.kt:39-41. Offer it only as an experimental owner option.
Taps falling through. The top ~8 % now exposes the full player's top bar. The scrim must consume every pointer and dismiss on tap, in both modes, or taps will hit the collapse and top-action buttons.

Removing glassQueueCoversPlayerProvider means the full player keeps drawing under the open queue (overdraw). Its lenses also re-render during every frame of the queue drag, because of the 0.972 scale. Realtime updates already stop at ≥8 % open (FullPlayerRuntimePolicy.kt:39), so the player is static at rest. Measure frame times on the Pixel 10 Pro.

The new ~92 % heavy lens (24/48 + depth) replaces the plain-backdrop GlassSheetScrim. It re-renders each frame while the sheet moves (open, drag, predictive-back scale) and is skipped while bloom is 0. AdaptiveModalBottomSheet sheets set the precedent, but this one is bigger. If it hitches, drop to a light panel (heavy = false).

Lens budget: the queue toolbar goes from 2 lenses to 4. The ⋯ morph adds 1 resizing lens plus 2 blooming pills for about 300 ms. Glass mode adds 2–3 lenses to the full player's song row. All are static at rest, but check gfxinfo.

The morph is custom code; no kit primitive does it. Layout-phase reads in glassMorphBounds must not leak into composition. The anchor must use positionInParent, not root coordinates, or it jitters while the sheet slides. The spring overshoot must be clamped for geometry. Back must close the menu before the queue (BackHandler at QueueBottomSheet.kt:294 already does this).

Never build glass pills on LiquidButton: it rebuilds drawBackdrop on every recomposition (LiquidButton.kt:84-135), which means a lens re-render per keystroke in Edit song and Save as playlist. Use GlassPanel, which memoises its modifier (GlassPanel.kt:102-176), and pass stable or rememberUpdatedState lambdas.

Material FAB menu: FloatingActionButtonMenu, ToggleFloatingActionButton and animateIcon were verified only by javap on the 1.5.0-alpha22 jar. Parameter names and defaults must be confirmed at compile time, and the alpha API may change. Anchoring it to the toolbar's ⋯ slot inside a fixed 70 dp Row needs the overlay-plus-layout approach, not a child of the Row, which would widen the Row and shift the toolbar.

Header inset: the status-bar padding at QueueBottomSheet.kt:803-805 has to be passed in. At 92 % on a short or landscape screen the sheet could reach under the status bar; resolveQueueSheetHeightPx clamps it.

Accessibility: the toolbar circles need `selected` semantics (previously only the icon description). The morph panel's label changes between 'More actions' and 'Save as playlist'. The disabled GlassPillButton needs explicit role and disabled semantics, because GlassPanel only adds a role when it has an onClick (GlassPanel.kt:193-203). Check with TalkBack.

File overlap with other Android items: player-controls (FullPlayerContent.kt, UnifiedPlayerSheet*), sync-editor (EditSongSheet / SongInfoBottomSheet presentation), and accent-color (GlassPalette.accent drives the pill and lit tints). Land in an agreed order or rebase carefully.

ownerDecisions:
Queue 'see-through' on Android. Android glass refracts only the album-art background, never the app behind it.
(a) Recommended: a ~92 % glass sheet over that background, with the player visible above it under a light scrim.
(b) Experimental: sample the frozen player so its art and controls show through the glass. Higher GPU cost, and it breaks the kit's no-glass-on-glass rule.
(c) Keep today's full-height queue.
Material mode queue: also make it ~92 % tall with the player peeking above under the scrim (recommended, same feature in Material style), or keep it full height?

Material mode ⋯ menu: switch to Material 3's FAB menu, where the ⋯ button morphs into a close button and the actions spring out of it (recommended Material equivalent of the glass morph)? Or keep today's centred pills over the scrim?
Material mode queue toolbar: keep the current capsule with tonal circles (recommended; the separate-circles change is glass-only) or split it into separate tonal circles too?
Edit song: make Cancel a neutral glass pill as well as Save (recommended, matches iOS), or only Save?

Audit scope for this wave. The full player's lyrics, Taizo and buffering chips are still solid fills in glass mode (the most visible leftover). Also convert the screen FABs (Genre options, Daily Mix AI, Create/Save playlist) to glass orbs or pills? Recommended: yes to both. The Daily Mix star-shaped FAB would become a round glass orb.

Listening Stats and the song options, AI Daily Mix and Taizo sheets already match the requested look on Android: Stats uses the same glass bar as Settings, and the sheets are already partial-height glass. Confirm no change is needed there.
tests: New JVM test QueueSheetGeometryTest: resolveQueueSheetHeightPx gives 0.92×H on a tall screen, clamps to H − statusTop − 8 dp on a short screen, never goes negative, and the hidden offset is height + bottom padding.
New JVM test GlassMorphMathTest: lerpMorphRect endpoints, midpoint and overshoot clamp; morphFadeOut / morphFadeIn curves are monotonic and bounded.
New JVM test GlassPillButtonTest: glassPillTint is accent@0.38 only when prominent and enabled, tintSubtle otherwise, for both GlassPalette.Dark and GlassPalette.Light.
Regression: `./gradlew :app:testDebugUnitTest`. Existing GlassAdoptionTest, GlassKitMathTest, GlassShellGeometryTest, GlassPaletteTest and PlayerBottomAnchoringTest must stay green.
Build: `./gradlew :app:assembleDebug`. With the default ABI splits the APK is app/build/outputs/apk/debug/app-arm64-v8a-debug.apk.

Performance on device, only with permission: `adb shell dumpsys gfxinfo com.theveloper.pixelplay.debug framestats` during queue open/close, queue drag and the ⋯ morph, compared with the current build. Look for janky frames from the full-player overdraw and the 92 % lens.
